claim.claim-text: 1. A system (300) comprising:

2. The system (300) of Claim 1, wherein: the translucent display (105) includes a display face (110) and a projection face (115), wherein the at least one projector (125) is configured to project the at least one image (130) on the projection face (115) of the translucent display (105), and wherein the at least one image (130) is displayed on the display face (110); and, optionally, the at least one projector (125) is configured to project the at least one image (130) on the projection face (115) in reverse such that the at least one image (130) is displayed in proper orientation on the display face (110).

3. The system (300) of Claim 1 or 2, wherein the stowable support surface is affixed to a wall (705), and wherein the at least one projector (125) is positioned on an opposite side of the wall (705) as the stowable support surface.
4. The system (300) of Claim 3 further comprising:

a lens (710) affixed in the wall (705), wherein the at least one projector (125) projects the at least one image (130) through the lens (710) to the translucent display (105); and, optionally, a mirror positioned on a projector side of the wall (705), wherein the mirror is configured to receive the at least one image (130) from the at least one projector (125) and transmit the at least one image (130) through the lens (710) to the translucent display (105).
5. The system (300) of Claim 4, wherein the lens (710) further includes a shutter (712), wherein the projector controller (135) is further programmed to:

instruct the at least one projector (125) to open the shutter (712) when the stowable support surface is in the first position; and instruct the at least one projector (125) to close the shutter (712) when the stowable support surface is not in the first position.
6. The system (300) of any of Claims 1-5, wherein the projector controller (135) is further programmed to:

receive a signal from the at least one sensor (305) indicating that the stowable support surface is in the first position; and instruct the at least one projector (125) to resume projection of images (130).
7. The system (300) of any of Claims 1-6, wherein the at least one projector (125) is configured to project one of a series of images (130) and a video.
8. The system (300) of any of Claims 1-7, wherein:
the stowable support surface includes a translucent projection area (720) and a surrounding border area (715); and the at least one image (130) is projected on the translucent projection area (720).
9. The system (300) of Claim 8, wherein: the translucent projection area (720) is recessed in relation to the surrounding border area (715).
10. A lavatory (1200) comprising the system of any of claim 1 to 9.

11. A method for operating a projector system (300), where the method is implemented by a computing device (135) comprising at least one processor (1705) in communication with at least one memory device (1710), the method comprising:
12. The method of Claim 11, further comprising:

receiving a third signal from the second sensor (305) indicating that the stowable support surface is in the stowed position; and transmitting instructions to the first projector (125) to resume projection of the first projection sequence.
13. The method of Claim 12, wherein:

transmitting instructions to the first projector (125) to project the first projection sequence onto a projection face (115) of the first translucent display (105) further comprises transmitting instructions to the first projector (125) and a second projector (125) associated with a second translucent display (105) to display the first projection sequence on the display face (110) of the first translucent display (105) and the second translucent display (105), such that the first projection sequence is displayed on a display face (110) of the second translucent display (105), wherein the second translucent display (105) is different from the first translucent display (105); and the method further comprises: transmitting instructions to the first projector (125) to halt projection of the first projection sequence in response to the second signal while the second projector (125) continues to project the first projection sequence on the second translucent display (105); and, optionally, synchronizing the display of the first projection sequence by first projector (125) and the second projector (125).
14. The method of any of Claim 12 or 13, wherein:
the first sensor (305) is a door lock sensor (305); and, optionally, the method further comprises:
receiving a third signal from the first sensor (305) indicating that a door lock has been unlocked; and instructing the first projector (125) to activate a sleep mode.

15. The method of any of Claims 11-14, wherein the second sensor (305) is one of a proximity switch, a magnetic switch, a level switch, a tilt/displacement switch a radial switch, a mercury switch, and a latch sensor (305).
